newsitem.title: USA: Ex-MGM head gets two weeks to return to U.S.A..
newsitem.headline: Ex-MGM head gets two weeks to return to U.S.A..

text.p: A Delaware judge on Friday gave former Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc owner Giancarlo Parretti two weeks to return from Italy for sentencing on a conviction of perjury and evidence tampering.
In a court hearing on whether Parretti should forfeit bail after failing to appear for sentencing on Jan. 6, Parretti's lawyer said arrangements were being made for his return.

Delaware Superior Court Judge Richard Cooch said he would give Parretti until Feb. 7 to show up, after prosecutor Paul Wallace said he would agree to the extension and not seek immediate forfeiture of $10,000 cash bail.
"We'll give him two weeks...to put up or shut up. At the end, we'll...go full steam ahead with the U.S. Attorney's office in Los Angeles to bring Mr. Parretti back," Wallace said.
Parretti was found guilty in November of the charges that stemmed from a 1991 legal battle with Frech bank Credit Lyonnais over control of MGM.

He faces a prison term of up to 10 years. But shortly before Parretti was due to be sentenced, his Italian lawyer notified the Delaware court that Parretti had returned to Italy to deal with tax charges pending against him.
His Delaware lawyer, Eugene Maurer, told Reuters that the Italian lawyer may have "incorrectly" advised Parretti.
If he does not return, Parretti could also lose $100,000 bail secured by real estate in California.

That bail was posted while he appealed a federal court ruling in Los Angeles that he be extradited to France to face charges of fraud and embezzlement related to his purchase of MGM with a $1.3 billion loan from a subsidiary of Credit Lyonnais, which ousted him from MGM in 1991.

If Parretti returns voluntarily before Feb. 7, a new sentencing date will be set, deputy attorney general Julie Flanigan told Reuters. If not, the bail forfeiture hearing will resume on Feb. 7 in Delaware.
Parretti also has a $3.9 billion lawsuit pending in California against Credit Lyonnais, alleging the bank conspired to take MGM away from him.
